ideas.title: Sluice Row
ideas.novelty_gate_note: Search for 'mancala variant pit capacity gauge skip full pit graduated seed sizes value' surfaced only standard Kalah/Oware/Bao/Congkak/Igisoro/Isolo descriptions, none combining a physical fill-line skip rule with graduated seed values. Claim not contradicted.
ideas.geometric_tooling_note: Ranks 2 (capacity_ring), 3 (seed_small), and 4 (store_pit) all came back 'unbindable' ('no geometry could be bound to the named part(s)'). For ranks 2 and 4 this is correct: project/main.py cuts the capacity rings and the two store wells directly into the single trough_board solid via boolean subtraction, so no separately-named part exists for the checker to bind to -- a genuine pipeline limitation (subtractive features on a monolithic board are never separately addressable). Rank 3 is different and likely a scorer defect, not a geometry defect: content.json and the STEP file list both show seed_small_01..16 present as 16 distinct, correctly-named top-level assembly parts, and they are clearly visually distinguishable by diameter in every render examined -- the 'unbindable' verdict for this rank does not match the artifacts. Scored as reported (fail, 0 credit) per the rule that geometric status is consumed, not re-derived, but flagged here and in PAIN_POINTS.md.
ideas.printability_disagreement_note: Independent printability_0_10 (evaluation_report.json) = 8.23 (class 'easy' for every individual part, 'hard'/7.5 for the assembly owing to '49 disconnected mesh components') vs. pipeline's own review_fix.printability = 10 (job_result, printability-only mode, 0 iterations). 49/49 is the correct, intended component count (board + 48 loose seed-weights, matching the rank-1 pass), so this is not the fusion signature CAD_GRAMMAR.md warns about -- it is the same pattern CAD_GRAMMAR.md already documents for t14: the independent scorer flags a real multi-body print-planning risk factor that the pipeline's own printability-only grader is blind to.
ideas.playability_check: No zeroing or Fidelity penalty applied. Small wells are 26mm dia x 16mm deep; the 7mm-tall seed-weights sit flush on the floor, so their top surface sits 9mm below the rim with zero protrusion above the board surface -- well within a normal fingertip pinch-and-lift (Kalah-style pits routinely run this deep) and nowhere near the ~60mm finger-room budget being exceeded. Board is a single flat layer with no stacking or overhangs, so every well and both store wells are fully visible to a seated player from directly above. Reach and sight both clear.
